notes: Situations written by Claude for this game: at least two options per stage that trade different resources (gold, HP, time, skill), asymmetric options that favour particular builds, and two wonders. Three follow-ups (sold-out-ambush, creeping-fever, wardens-on-your-trail) serve the twist table. biomes (Plan 3) limit where three situations are drawn on the road. Every situation has a disposition (hostile, neutral or pleasant) for travel pace. Three follow-ups that hunt the party (sold-out-ambush, wardens-on-your-trail, grudge-on-the-road) are flagged pursuit: the pace since they were queued decides whether they catch up. Four sea situations (squall-off-the-bow, passenger-overboard, something-under-the-hull, smugglers-below-decks) are the only ones drawn at sea; smugglers-below-decks is tagged brawl, so a stowaway's critical failure starts it. Seven road situations (ambush-at-the-narrows, mapmakers-apprentice, hedge-witch, pilgrims-at-dusk, flooded-ferry, lizardfolk-herb, wardens-on-your-trail) leave a clue on success: a discoverPoi effect that reveals a nearby point of interest (Plan 3b B3). Plan 4 (B5): consumables unlock surer or easier options, and each one is spent by the option that needs it: a gear line across the flooded ferry, healing kits for the hedge-witch, the creeping fever and the burning barn, alchemist's fire at the narrows and on the sea, and an arcana warding against the ghoul pilgrims. Five new road situations: horse-thieves (thieves who lead off a stealable animal and take a share of precious goods), cutpurse-at-the-fair (thieves), toll-bridge and tribute-at-the-pass (tolls in gold or goods), and barn-on-fire. ambush-at-the-narrows is now tagged thieves. Reputation effects (standing with the nearby settlement) reward helping locals and punish wronging them: mapmakers-apprentice, grudge-on-the-road, wardens-on-your-trail, horse-thieves, toll-bridge, cutpurse-at-the-fair and barn-on-fire. tavern-brawl (weight 0, tagged tavern-trouble) is never drawn on the road: only a critical failure listening for rumours starts it. After a failed talk or detour against a hostile group, the other is gone too (a shared once group, "get-past"): ambush-at-the-narrows's veiled threat joins the hostile-group archetype's Slip past and Parley, and tribute-at-the-pass pairs the stare-down with the goat tracks.

start.text: Spring melt has swollen the river to a brown roar. The ferry rope still holds, and so does the ferrywoman, Ilse, who has tripled her price and isn't ashamed of it.

outcome.text: Ilse counts the coins, spits for luck, and hauls you across.

options.label: Haggle
options.description: She enjoys a haggle. She also enjoys winning one.

fail.text: Ilse folds her arms. The price stands.

partial.text: She knocks a little off, muttering.

success.text: Ilse laughs and takes half. While she poles you over, she tells you what the flood turned up downriver.

critSuccess.text: Ilse takes you across for a song. {actor} has to sing it, all the way over.

options.label: Ford the river upstream
options.description: Free, if the river lets you.

critFail.text: The current takes {actor} off their feet and a long way downstream. You find them half-drowned an hour later.

fail.text: Halfway across, the bottom drops away.

partial.text: You make it across, soaked and shaking.

success.text: {actor} finds the shallows and leads you over.

options.label: Rig a line across (1 gear)
options.description: Rope and pitons make the ford a far safer bet. The river keeps the rope.

fail.text: The line holds, just. You haul yourselves over hand over hand, half drowned.

partial.text: {actor} gets the line across on the second try, and you cross wet to the waist.

success.text: {actor} swims the line over and makes it fast. You cross dry-shod, and Ilse swears at you from her ferry.

options.label: Wait for the water to drop

outcome.text: Two days of drizzle and bad food in Ilse's lean-to. Then the river calms, and she takes you over at her usual price.

midstream.text: The river has you. Your packs drag at you, and the far bank is still a long way off.

options.label: Swim for it
options.description: Keep your packs and fight the current for the far bank.

fail.text: You crawl out a mile downstream, battered by every rock in the river.

partial.text: You make the bank, minus a pack.

success.text: {actor} drags everyone to the far bank.

outcome.text: You let the river have your packs, and the coin in them, and swim free.

entries.title: The hedge-witch's price
entries.notes: Most useful when the party is hurt. Arcana-heavy parties get a cheaper deal.

start.text: Smoke rises from a turf hut at the edge of the bog. The old woman inside looks at your wounds before she looks at your faces. 'I can mend that,' she says. 'Everything has a price.'

outcome.text: She takes the silver without looking at it and smears something green into your cuts.

options.label: Work it off
options.description: A day of cutting turf and hauling water.

outcome.text: A long day cutting turf and hauling water. That night she sees to your wounds.

options.label: Trade her a secret of the craft
options.description: She collects spells the way magpies collect spoons.

fail.text: She isn't impressed. 'Coin or sweat,' she says.

partial.text: She takes the lore, grudgingly, and does half the job.

success.text: Her eyes light up. She mends you, sends you off with her blessing, and tells you of a place she'd rather you bothered than her.

options.label: Pay her in bandages (1 healing)
options.description: She is short of clean linen and salves. A kit buys her best work.

outcome.text: She sniffs the salve, approves, and uses half of it on you. The rest goes on her shelf.
She shrugs and goes back to her pot.

twist.what: the pilgrims are ghoul-touched, and hungry for more than bread

start.text: At dusk, three pilgrims in grey ask to share your fire. They are polite and hungry, and one of them never seems to blink.

outcome.text: You make room. They eat like they haven't in weeks, and say little.

options.label: Watch them over the fire
options.description: Insight shows how likely the worst is. Misreading them puts you off your next move.

critFail.text: {actor} stares too long. The pilgrims fall silent and stare back, and {actor} reads it all wrong.

fail.text: Grief, maybe. Or hunger. {actor} settles on the wrong answer.

partial.text: Something about them is wrong. {actor} can't say how wrong.

success.text: {actor} studies them over the fire and gets the measure of them.

outcome.text: They bow and walk on into the dark. You sleep badly, but you sleep.

twist.text: They bow and walk on into the dark. Later, you hear something screaming, far down the road.

night.text: The fire burns low. The pilgrims sleep, or seem to.

outcome.text: You wake at dawn to find them gone, and a sprig of rowan tucked into each of your packs.

twist.text: You wake to cold hands and teeth.

options.label: Keep watch through the night
options.description: Costs someone a night's sleep.

fail.text: {actor} nods off. At dawn the pilgrims are gone.

twist.text: {actor} nods off, and wakes to teeth.

partial.text: A long, cold night. At dawn the pilgrims are gone.

twist.text: {actor} sees them rise just in time.

success.text: {actor} keeps a sharp watch. At dawn the pilgrims leave rowan sprigs by the fire, and directions to the shrine they are walking to.

twist.text: {actor} sees them rise, grey and silent, and shouts the camp awake.

options.label: Ward the camp with salt and chalk (1 arcana)
options.description: A circle nothing dead can cross. Whatever they are, you all sleep.

outcome.text: You draw the circle round your bedrolls, and the pilgrims watch you do it without a word. At dawn they are gone.

twist.text: At midnight the pilgrims rise, grey and silent, and stop at the chalk line. They circle until dawn, hissing, then slink off down the road.

attack.text: The pilgrims are on you, grey-skinned and silent, with nails like hooks.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Stand your ground against their hooked nails.

fail.text: You drive them off, but their touch leaves you numb and torn.

partial.text: You drive them off into the dark.

success.text: You put them down. Their purses hold old, grave-cold coins.

options.label: Grab what you can and run
options.description: Snatch up what you can and run for the dark. Something may be left behind.

fail.text: They drag at you as you go, and you drop half your coin.

partial.text: You get away, leaving half your camp behind.

success.text: You run, and they don't follow past the firelight.

start.text: The road squeezes between two boulders, and {foe} step out to fill the gap. Their leader grins and nods at your packs.

options.label: A quiet word about the last lot
options.description: Intimidation (CHA): a calm, specific threat. Better from a silver tongue than a big arm.

fail.text: Their leader laughs. 'Nice try.'

partial.text: They let you pass, but they'll remember your faces.

success.text: {actor}'s quiet words do what swords couldn't. They melt back into the rocks, and {actor} marks which way they go.

critSuccess.text: They melt back into the rocks, and one of them leaves an apology in silver. {actor} marks which way they go.

options.label: Throw alchemist's fire (1 alchemicals)
options.description: Fire in a narrow place breaks a line fast. The flask is gone either way.

fail.text: The flask bursts short. They come through the smoke, and it's a brawl after all.

partial.text: The fire splits them. You force the gap, singed, and leave them beating at their cloaks.

success.text: {actor}'s flask lands square among them. They scatter screaming, and drop what they'd already taken from others.

entries.title: The mapmaker's apprentice

twist.what: the 'apprentice' is the thief, and his friends are waiting for whoever stops to help

start.text: A young man in ink-stained sleeves sits by a broken surveying tripod, crying with rage. His master's instruments were stolen in the night, he says, and he will be beaten for it.

options.label: Follow the thieves' trail
options.description: Survival-minded parties can sort this out properly, for a day's work.

fail.text: The trail goes cold in the bracken. A wasted day.

twist.text: The trail loops back to the boy, and his friends are waiting for {actor}.

partial.text: You find the instruments dumped in a ditch, half of them broken. He pays what he can.

success.text: You find the thieves' camp and take the instruments back. His master pays well, lets you copy a page of his survey, and tells the whole town who helped.

twist.text: The trail loops straight back to the 'apprentice', and you come up behind his waiting friends.

ambush.text: His friends step out of the bracken with cudgels, and the 'apprentice' wipes his eyes, grins and joins them.

entries.notes: A bespoke twist: every twist escalates into the 'ambush' stage, with footing set by how you helped.

entries.title: An old grudge
entries.notes: Queued when you exploit someone in need (the someone-in-need archetype) or leave a threat hanging.

start.text: Someone you wronged on the road has not forgotten. They are waiting at the next bridge, with two cousins and a cudgel each.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Three of them, angry rather than skilled.

fail.text: You win, but the cudgels find their mark first.

partial.text: They go into the river, and {actor} nearly goes with them.

success.text: They go into the river. The bridge-keeper pretends not to see, but word of it gets about.

outcome.text: You pay back what you took, and a little more, in front of the whole bridge. They spit, but they let it go, and the locals see you settle your debts.

options.label: Apologise, and mean it
options.description: Words instead of coin or cudgels. They may want more than words.

fail.text: They are not interested in words.

partial.text: They take the apology, and some coin to go with it.

success.text: They grumble, but let you pass. Maybe it ends here.

options.label: Take the ford instead
options.description: Avoid the bridge by the slippery stones downstream. You lose them, or a day.

fail.text: They catch {actor} on the slippery stones.

partial.text: You lose them, and most of a day, in the reeds.

success.text: You are across the ford before they can reach it.

start.text: As the marsh grows dark, the reeds light up: thousands of moths, each carrying a cold spark, rise in slow spirals over the water.

options.label: Watch until the last light fades

outcome.text: For a while nobody speaks. Later, nobody can agree on how long you stood there.

start.text: On the ridge, a ring of standing stones hums in the wind, each a different note. Together they almost make a tune you know.

outcome.text: You stop and listen until the wind changes. The tune stays with you for days.

entries.title: The lizardfolk's herb
entries.notes: Follow-up completing the trade in the ported 'lizardfolk-ritual' (data/original).

start.text: Two days on, you find the jungle the lizardfolk spoke of: wet green dark, loud with insects. Somewhere in here grows the herb they want.

options.label: Search for the herb
options.description: Comb the wet dark for the herb. The jungle charges by the day.

critFail.text: {actor} brushes a nettle-vine that leaves an arm numb and swollen. No herb.

fail.text: A day of searching, and nothing to show for it. The herb is still out there.

partial.text: You find it after a long, leech-ridden day. The lizardfolk keep their word: the artifact is yours.

effects.text: Weather-calling artifact (items arrive in a later plan).

success.text: You find the herb at the foot of a drowned tree, and through the green beyond it, carved stones. The lizardfolk keep their word: the artifact is yours.

effects.text: Weather-calling artifact (items arrive in a later plan).

outcome.text: You leave the herb to the jungle, and the artifact to the lizardfolk.

entries.title: A route sold
entries.notes: Queued by the informant twist (twists.json): a deadlier ambush that knows you are coming.

start.text: Your route was sold. {Raiders} are waiting at the one place where the road can't be left, and they know exactly what you carry.

options.label: Spot their lookouts first
options.description: Whatever you do next goes better if you see them first.

fail.text: A lookout whistles before {actor} sees him. They know you've seen the trap.

partial.text: {actor} spots one lookout, too late to matter.

success.text: {actor} finds the lookouts before they find you. Now you choose how this starts.

entries.title: The fever comes back
entries.notes: Queued by the contagion twist (twists.json) when the fever is ignored or badly treated.

start.text: The fever you shrugged off has come back, and brought friends. By noon, two of you are shivering in the saddle.

options.label: Nurse it yourselves
options.description: Find the right herb yourselves. No coin spent, if it works.

fail.text: Nothing {actor} tries helps. It burns through you all before it breaks.

partial.text: {actor} keeps it in check. A day lost to sweating it out.

success.text: {actor} finally finds the right herb. The fever breaks overnight.

outcome.text: Two long days under a hedge, and then it's over.
A village healer takes your coin and gives you something vile. It works.

options.label: Dose them from the kit (1 healing)
options.description: Willow bark and fever-salts from your own packs. Sure, and no day lost.

outcome.text: Bitter tea and cold cloths. By evening the shivering stops, and you walk on in the morning.
You march through it, and it takes it out of you.

entries.title: Wardens on your trail
entries.notes: Queued by the fugitive twist (twists.json) when you lied for or ran with the runaway.

start.text: Riders in the duke's colours catch up with you at a ford. They know you helped the runaway, and they want a word, or a fine, or both.

outcome.text: The captain counts it slowly and lets you go.

options.label: Talk your way out
options.description: Convince the captain you were fooled like everyone else.

fail.text: The captain has heard it all before.

partial.text: They settle for a smaller fine.

success.text: {actor} convinces the captain you were fooled like everyone else. Mollified, he tells you where the real outlaws are camped, in case you want to be useful.

options.label: Make a run for it
options.description: Splash across the ford before they turn their horses.

fail.text: They ride you down in the shallows.

partial.text: You lose them in the reeds, and most of a day with them.

success.text: You're over the ford and into the woods before they turn their horses.

options.label: Fight them
options.description: Trained riders, and the duke will hear of it.

fail.text: Trained riders against tired travellers. You get away, barely.

partial.text: You unhorse two, and the rest decide you aren't worth it. The duke's people won't forget it.

success.text: You send them back to the duke with bruised pride and lighter purses. Every town on this road will hear who did it.

entries.title: A squall off the bow
entries.notes: Strong backs earn back part of the fare; a weather eye can spare everyone the worst; hiding below costs a day.

start.text: The sky to windward goes the colour of a bruise. Within the hour the squall is on you: rain flying sideways, the deck tilting, and the bosun bellowing for every pair of hands.

options.label: Haul on the lines with the crew
options.description: Hard, wet work. The captain remembers who helped.

critFail.text: A wave takes {actor}'s feet from under them and slams them into the rail.

fail.text: {actor} hangs on, but a loose block cracks them across the shoulder.

partial.text: You keep the sail from tearing loose, at the cost of skinned palms all round.

success.text: {actor} is first to the lines and last to leave them. When the sky clears, the captain hands back part of your fare.

critSuccess.text: {actor} spots a parting halyard just before it goes and saves the mainsail. The captain hands back your fare and pours you his good rum.

options.label: Read the weather for the captain
options.description: Call the turn early and the worst passes astern. Call it wrong and you sail into it.

fail.text: {actor} calls the turn the wrong way, and the ship runs straight into the heart of it.

partial.text: {actor} calls the turn late. It takes the edge off the squall, but there is still work on deck.

success.text: {actor} reads the cloud and calls the turn early. The squall passes astern with barely a drop on deck.

critSuccess.text: {actor} calls the turn early, and the captain, impressed, refuses to hear of a fare for the rest of the voyage.

options.label: Wait it out below decks
options.description: Safe, but with fewer hands the ship runs before the wind and loses a day.

outcome.text: You wedge yourselves between the cargo and listen to the hull groan all night. By morning the ship is far off its course.

entries.title: Passenger overboard
entries.notes: A swimmer earns the reward and risks the sea; a sharp eye earns less safely; or let the crew deal with it.

start.text: A shriek from the stern. A merchant's boy has gone over the rail, and the ship is already leaving him behind. The crew are slow with the boat; his father is not slow to wave his purse.

options.label: Dive in after him
options.description: Fast, and dangerous in this swell.

critFail.text: The swell drives {actor} under twice. The crew haul out the boy and then {actor}, half-drowned.

fail.text: {actor} reaches him, but the sea fights them all the way back, and in the end it is the crew's boat that brings them in. The father's thanks are warm; his purse stays shut.

partial.text: {actor} gets him back, having swallowed half the sea. The father pays, if less than he waved.

success.text: {actor} has the boy back aboard before the crew have the boat untied. His father empties his purse into {actor}'s wet hands.

critSuccess.text: {actor} has the boy back aboard before the crew have the boat untied. His father empties his purse, and the whole ship drinks to {actor} that night.

options.label: Keep him in sight and guide the boat
options.description: Safer. Someone has to watch where he went under.

fail.text: You lose him in the swell for a long minute. The boat finds him in the end, no thanks to you.

partial.text: {actor} points the boat to him, a little late. The boy comes back cold and frightened, and his father presses a few coins on you.

success.text: {actor} never takes their eyes off him and calls the boat straight to him. His father is grateful.

outcome.text: The crew get the boat over at last, and the boy lives. His father does not look at you again for the rest of the voyage.

entries.title: Something under the hull
entries.notes: Stealth, a harpoon, silver for the sea, or a flask of alchemist's fire. The harpoon pays and can go badly; the flask is sure but costs 20 gp of goods for a 5 gp thank-you.

start.text: The ship shudders, then shudders again. Something long and dark is passing under the keel, and the sailors have gone very quiet. One of them is fingering a harpoon.

options.label: Keep still and quiet
options.description: Old sailors say it hunts by sound.

critFail.text: Someone drops a pail. A coil as thick as a mast breaks the water and sweeps the deck before it sinks away.

fail.text: A loose block knocks against the rail. The ship lurches as the thing rises to look, and someone is thrown against the hatch.

partial.text: It circles once more, then sinks away, and a barrel of your stores goes with it, torn from its lashings.

success.text: It loses interest and sinks back into the dark.

critSuccess.text: It rises close enough to show one vast, ancient eye, looks at you for a long moment, and goes. Nobody speaks for a long time.

options.label: Help the sailor drive it off
options.description: If it takes the iron, the crew will stand you a share of the fare.

critFail.text: The harpoon line snaps taut and drags {actor} the length of the deck.

fail.text: The iron glances off. The thing shoulders the hull hard enough to spring a plank, and everyone bails until dawn.

partial.text: It takes the iron and dives, and the line burns through {actor}'s hands.

success.text: {actor}'s throw goes deep. The thing thrashes and is gone, and the crew roar and pass the hat.

critSuccess.text: {actor}'s throw goes deep, and the thing is gone for good. The captain hands back your fare and the crew pass the hat as well.

options.label: Give the sea its due
options.description: The sailors swear by an offering of silver.

outcome.text: You throw a handful of silver over the side and the sailors nod. Whether by luck or by custom, it sinks away.

options.label: Pour alchemist's fire on the water (1 alchemicals)
options.description: Nothing that lives in the deep likes burning water over its head.

outcome.text: The flask bursts on the swell and the sea burns green. Something huge flinches away beneath it, and does not come back. The crew stand you a share of the fare.

entries.title: Smugglers below decks
entries.notes: Tagged brawl: a stowaway's critical failure starts it (travel/stowaway.ts). Fists, a convincing lie, or coin; a half-believed lie follows you ashore.

start.text: Below decks, among crates that are plainly not salt fish, a knot of sailors closes in with belaying pins in their fists. They would rather you went over the side than ashore talking.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Sailors brawl dirty, and there are more of them.

critFail.text: They beat you to the deck and go through your purses before the mate breaks it up.

fail.text: You hold them off until the mate breaks it up, and every one of you is bruised and bleeding.

partial.text: A short, ugly fight in the dark. {actor} takes the worst of it.

success.text: {actor} drops the biggest of them, and the rest lose their nerve.

critSuccess.text: {actor} lays out two of them, and the rest suddenly want to be friends. Friends who share.

options.label: Swear you saw nothing
options.description: Talk them round. If they half believe you, they will be waiting in port.

critFail.text: Nobody believes a word, and now they are angry as well. Someone swings first.

fail.text: They aren't convinced, and they close in.

partial.text: They let you be for now, but you catch them watching you all the way to port.

success.text: {actor} convinces them you can't tell salt fish from brandy. They laugh and leave you be.

critSuccess.text: {actor} convinces them so well that they cut you in for your silence.

options.label: Pay for your silence
options.description: Coin talks louder than promises.

outcome.text: They count it twice, and leave you be.

entries.title: Thieves in the night
entries.notes: Thieves come for the animals and the precious goods. A loss without a named animal takes the most valuable stealable ones; precious goods go by fraction. A party with neither loses nothing to them, but still has to deal with the knives.

start.text: A hoof stamps in the dark, and a hand is already in your packs. Shadows are cutting your picket line, and someone is whispering to the animals to keep them quiet.

options.label: Rush them
options.description: Steel in the dark. Keep what's yours if you're quick enough.

critFail.text: A knife finds {actor} in the dark, and by the time you have a light lit they are gone, with an animal and a share of your goods.

fail.text: You trade blows with shadows. They get away with an animal on a lead.

partial.text: You save the animals, but one of them was already off with a pack of your precious goods.

success.text: {actor} is among them before they know it. They flee empty-handed into the dark.

critSuccess.text: {actor} knocks one flat. He wakes up tied to a tree, and his purse pays for your trouble.

options.label: Raise the camp and light the fires
options.description: Thieves hate light and noise. Safer than steel, if everyone wakes fast.

fail.text: By the time the fire catches, they've gone, and so has an animal and a share of your goods.

partial.text: The fire flares up and they scatter, but a pack goes with them.

success.text: {actor} spots them first and roars the camp awake. They bolt without a thing.

options.label: Lie still and let them take it
options.description: Nobody gets stabbed. Everything else is negotiable.

outcome.text: You lie still and listen to them work. They are thorough, and they take their time.

trail.text: At first light the trail is plain: hoofprints and boot-marks, heading for the nearest village's back roads.

options.label: Track them down
options.description: A day's work. What they've already sold is gone, but their purse is not.

fail.text: The trail splits and splits again. You lose a day and find nothing.

partial.text: You find their fire still warm and a purse they forgot in a hurry.

success.text: {actor} runs them to ground in a byre. You take their takings, and the village reeve thanks you for ridding the road of them.

options.label: Cut your losses and move on

outcome.text: You repack what's left and take the road, a little lighter.

entries.title: The toll bridge
entries.notes: A lord's toll in coin or in kind. Arguing the charter or slipping across at night is free if it works; a fine and a black mark with the locals if it doesn't. The ford costs a day.

start.text: A stone bridge with a gatehouse squats over a fast river. A bored toll-keeper in a lord's livery eyes your packs and names a price, then a higher one when he sees what's in them.

outcome.text: He bites a coin, writes you in his book, and lifts the bar.

options.label: Pay in kind (1 luxuries)
options.description: He'll take a bolt of silk or a cask of wine for his lord's cellar, and fewer questions.

outcome.text: His eyes light up at the wine. He waves you through without writing anything down.

options.label: Argue the old charter
options.description: Travellers on the king's business pass free. Are you? Can you sound like it?

fail.text: He's heard that one. Now the price includes his trouble.

partial.text: He doesn't believe you, but he halves it to be rid of you.

success.text: {actor} quotes the charter at him until he lifts the bar to make it stop.

options.label: Slip across after dark
options.description: Free if nobody sees. If they do, the lord's men fine you, and the locals hear of it.

fail.text: A dog barks, a lantern swings, and you are fined on the spot in front of half the village.

partial.text: You get across, but the keeper sees your backs and shouts after you. Word will get round.

success.text: {actor} leads you over under the gatehouse's nose.

options.label: Go round by the ford
options.description: A day downstream and back.

outcome.text: A long wet day to a ford and back to the road. The toll-keeper waves as you pass on the far bank.

entries.title: A cutpurse at the fair
entries.notes: A crossroads fair is a good place to sell and a better one to be robbed. Catching the cutpurse leads to a choice between the reeve's thanks (reputation), a bribe (gold), or rough justice (gold, but the locals turn against you).

start.text: A crossroads fair has sprung up in a meadow: stalls, pipers, a dancing bear, and a crowd thick enough to lose a purse in. Someone small and quick is already brushing past your packs.

options.label: Browse the stalls, one eye on your packs
options.description: Good bargains, if you can keep your goods.

fail.text: By evening you notice the slit in the pack. Some of your best goods are somewhere in the crowd.

partial.text: {actor} feels the tug too late. A purse is gone, but the packs are whole.

success.text: {actor} catches a thin wrist halfway into your pack, and holds on.

options.label: Take turns guarding the packs
options.description: Safe, slow, and you see half the fair each.

outcome.text: One of you sits on the packs while the others wander. Nothing goes missing, but the fair takes all day.

options.label: Skirt the crowd and keep going

outcome.text: You keep to the edge of the meadow and the road beyond it.

caught.text: The cutpurse is a wiry youth with a fistful of your goods and a face full of fear. People are turning to look. The reeve is somewhere nearby.

outcome.text: The reeve thanks you loudly, for the crowd's benefit. By nightfall half the fair knows your names.

options.label: Let them buy their way out

outcome.text: The youth empties a pouch into your hand and is gone into the crowd. Nobody else saw.

options.label: Teach them a lesson yourselves
options.description: Rough justice, and their purse besides. The crowd may not like it.

fail.text: The crowd turns on you, not the thief, who slips away in the shouting.

partial.text: You take their purse and frighten them half to death. The crowd mutters.

success.text: {actor} gives the youth a fright they won't forget, and takes their purse for the trouble. The crowd laughs.

entries.title: Tribute at the pass
entries.notes: A hill clan's road tax: coin, a share of the cargo (equipment and precious goods, and food for their pot), or a fight. Paying in kind is cheap for a poor party and dear for a laden one.

start.text: Where the road narrows into the pass, {foe} have built a wall of stacked stones with a gap just wide enough for a cart. 'Clan's road,' says their chief. 'Clan's tax.'

outcome.text: The chief weighs your purse in her hand and nods you through.

options.label: Let them take their pick of the cargo
options.description: They want weapons, armour, gear and anything that glitters, and food for their pot.

outcome.text: They go through your packs like a flock of crows: blades, rope, a jewelled thing, a sack of food. Then they wave you through, grinning.

options.label: Stare down the chief
options.description: Hill clans respect nerve. Show none and the price goes up.

fail.text: The chief laughs in your face. Now they want more, and they're ready for trouble.

partial.text: She respects the nerve, if not the threat, and takes a token tax.

success.text: {actor} doesn't blink. The chief spits, laughs, and lets you through for nothing. 'Next time, you pay double.'

options.label: Force the gap
options.description: They have the wall and the high ground.

critFail.text: They beat you back from the wall and take their tax from your fallen packs.

fail.text: You break through at last, bloodied, with stones bouncing after you.

partial.text: You force the gap. {actor} takes a club to the ribs on the way.

success.text: {actor} is over the wall before they are ready. They scatter, and leave the day's tax behind.

options.label: Find a way round by the goat tracks
options.description: Go round the wall by the herders' paths. Slow, if they are hard to find.

fail.text: The goat track ends at a cliff. Two days of scrambling before you find the road again.

partial.text: A long way round, but they never see you.

success.text: {actor} finds a herders' path over the shoulder of the hill.

entries.title: A barn on fire
entries.notes: Helping the locals costs HP, a healing kit or time and earns standing with the nearby town; looting while they're busy earns gold and loses it.

start.text: Smoke on the road ahead: a farm's barn is burning, the family is fighting it with buckets, and somewhere inside a horse is screaming. The farmhouse door stands open and unwatched.

options.label: Join the bucket line, and go in for the horse
options.description: Into the smoke for the horse. The farm won't forget it, either way.

fail.text: The roof comes down while {actor} is inside. You drag them out, burned and choking. The barn is lost, but the family won't forget you tried.

partial.text: The barn is lost, but {actor} leads the horse out through the smoke, singed and coughing.

success.text: You save the horse and half the barn. The farmer's wife feeds you, and her brother is a reeve in town.

options.label: Tend the burned (1 healing)
options.description: The farmer's boy is badly burned. A kit from your packs.

outcome.text: You salve and bind the boy's burns while the others fight the fire. The family can't pay, but they'll tell everyone.

options.label: Help yourselves at the farmhouse
options.description: Everyone's busy. Nobody would know. Probably.

fail.text: The farmer's daughter sees you coming out of the door with the strongbox. You drop it and run, and the story runs ahead of you.

partial.text: You get away with a few coins, and a neighbour's long, hard look at your faces.

success.text: The savings jar under the hearthstone, and nobody the wiser.

outcome.text: You walk on through the smoke. Nobody looks up as you pass.

entries.title: Trouble in the taproom
entries.notes: Never drawn on the road (weight 0): a critical failure listening for rumours at a tavern may start it (town/rumours.ts, tag tavern-trouble). Fists cost HP, talking it down costs a skill roll, and paying for the damage costs gold.

start.text: Someone at the next table decides your questions are an insult. A drover the size of a door pushes back his bench, his friends stand with him, and the keeper is already reaching under the bar for the cudgel.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Fists and chairs. Win, and the room is on your side.

critFail.text: You come to in the street, bruised all over, and someone has been through your purses.

fail.text: The keeper's cudgel ends it, and you are the ones thrown out.

partial.text: A short, ugly scuffle among the benches. {actor} takes the worst of it.

success.text: {actor} puts the drover on the floor, and his friends remember they were leaving.

critSuccess.text: {actor} lays the drover out with one blow. The room cheers, and the keeper stands you a round.

options.label: Talk him down
options.description: He is drunk, not stupid. Probably.

critFail.text: Whatever {actor} says, it is the wrong thing. He swings first.

fail.text: He isn't listening, and his friends are closing in.

partial.text: He sits down grumbling, once you have bought his table a round.

success.text: {actor} turns it into a joke, and by the end of it the drover is laughing too.

critSuccess.text: {actor} talks him round so well that he insists on buying the next round himself.

options.label: Pay for the damage and leave
options.description: Coin on the bar, and out the door before the first chair flies.

outcome.text: The keeper sweeps the coins off the bar and waves you out the back way.
